question: Why are learned feature representations more useful than raw pixels for downstream vision tasks?
direct_answer: Because good representations organize the input by semantic or task-relevant structure instead of by raw coordinate values.
expanded_answer: Raw pixels contain all image information, but much of it is irrelevant or poorly aligned with the task. A learned representation can compress away nuisance variation while preserving what matters, such as object identity, shape, or correspondence across views. That makes classification, detection, segmentation, and retrieval easier for a small downstream head or a fine-tuned model.
key_points: They improve transfer and downstream efficiency
common_wrong_ideas: Raw pixels are always enough if the model is big enough
A feature representation is only a compressed image
